new_statements.rule_in_words: No source states a positional stress rule for Milyan. The specialist literature treats Milyan as Lycian B, a dialect of Lycian, and characterizes Lycian (A and B jointly) as having a stress accent whose position is free/lexical (non-demarcative, largely columnar within paradigms), inherited from Proto-Anatolian; its location is recoverable only negatively, from prehistoric syncope (a syncopated vowel or a syllabic nasal m̃/ñ was unstressed). Milyan-specific evidence is limited to the same syncope/gemination facts (Shevoroshkin 2013: 157: geminates from loss of a neighbouring unstressed vowel; omitted vowel letters = reduction) and to individual Lycian B forms (trpplẽ < *tri-plóm; readers nouns in -ala- with suffixal, i.e. penultimate, accent per Billing). The metre of the two Milyan poems, the only potential direct evidence, is declared unsolved (Billing 2026).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing for Lycian/Milyan (Billing 2026: 'Lycian and Lydian: no positive evidence of cyclic stress effects (?)').
new_statements.exceptions: Billing: 'some cases of possible mobile accent' (Luwic-wide); Kloekhorst 2013: 143 mahana- nom.pl. mãhãi (2nd syllable unstressed, syncopated) vs dat.pl. mahãna (2nd syllable stressed) in Lycian A; Melchert 2004: 596 warns the syncope-based accent inference risks circularity.
new_statements.domain_note: Reconstructed word-level accent of an extinct epigraphic language; no orthographic marking of accent; evidence is diachronic (syncope outputs), not citation-form phonetics. Statement is made for 'Lycian' as a whole (A and B), with Lycian B forms among the examples.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources treat Milyan as 'Lycian B', a (more archaic, poetic) dialect of Lycian (lyci1241): Shevoroshkin 2013: 154 'фактически это архаический диалект ликийского языка'; Melchert 2004 describes Lycian A and Milyan jointly; Billing 2023/2026 speaks of 'Lycian' with 'two dialects: Lycian A (standard) vs. Lycian B (poetic; \"Milyan\")'. The quoted accent characterization is therefore for Lycian as a whole, with Lycian B forms (trpplẽ, trppala-, mutala-, xumala-, ziwala-, rm̃pala-) among the evidence; no Milyan-only accent rule exists in anything opened.

sources.note: Lycian = two dialects, 'Lycian A (standard) vs. Lycian B (poetic; "Milyan")'. Lycian accent located only by negative heuristics: 'If a vowel was syncopated, it did not carry the accent'; syllabic resonants m̃ ñ (l r) = unaccented; summary slide 'Lycian: Syncopated vowels = unaccented; Syllabic resonants = unaccented'. Lycian B readers-noun stems (mutala-, trppala-, xumala-, ziwala-, rm̃pala-) assigned 'penultimate' / 'penultimate or final' accent for the -ala- type; 'Lycian = penultimate accent' refers to that suffix type only.
